version: LOCK 37 V1 (9 Nov 2026) - Sahila and Sahila's boat
builds_on: LOCK 34 runner, LOCK 36 roads. Design reference (not shown): Bukhari 2079 (buyer and seller who speak the truth and make things clear are blessed).

sahila.name: Sahila
sahila.text: Where the river widens into a lake, fishing boats lie on the sand to dry and nets hang between poles. The whole shore smells of salt and smoke.

sahila.title: The shore masjid
sahila.text: Whitewashed walls, a floor of reed mats, and the sound of the water through the open door.
sahila.first: An old fisherman makes room for you in the row. “From Ilmara? Then you pray with us now.”

people.name: Mukhtar

lines.wary: Mukhtar sits by his boat, rubbing his knees. “Too old for the lake now. Too stubborn to stay off it.”
lines.friendly: “Forty years on that water. She has never thrown me in. Not once.”
lines.warm: “Sit with me. Tell me about Ilmara. I went once, as a boy.”

memory: “Fifty clean coins. My daughter says you were a fool. I say you were a friend.”
“Ziyad's boat took water. He came to my door. What could I tell him?”

people.name: Hind

lines.wary: Hind's needle flies through the net. “If you want fish, the market is over there.”
lines.friendly: “A torn net catches nothing. A torn word is the same.”
lines.warm: “My father talks about you. He doesn't talk about many people.”

memory: “You told Ziyad about the plank. I was angry for a day. Then I was glad.”

people.name: Ziyad

lines.wary: Ziyad looks you up and down. “Selling or buying?”
lines.friendly: “I buy boats, mend them, sell them up the river. Honest wood is hard to find.”
lines.warm: “If you ever sell me anything again, I won't even look at it. Your word is enough.”

memory: “The plank. You could have kept quiet. I've told every trader on this shore.”
“My boat sank at her mooring. You knew. Don't sell anything here again.”

missions.title: Sahila's boat
missions.button: Mukhtar wants to sell his boat

text: “My knees are done,” Mukhtar says. “I want to sell her, and I don't trust myself with traders - I'd give her away. River Market speaks for you. Sell her for me and keep five coins.”
Turning her over to clean her, you find one plank near the keel that is soft under the paint. She would float for a season, maybe two.

b.text: Ziyad the trader walks round the boat twice. “Eighty coins. Is she sound?”

choices.label: Tell him about the soft plank

text: Ziyad kneels and presses the plank. “Fifty, then. And I'll remember who told me.” Mukhtar takes the fifty coins and is quiet for a long time.
“Better fifty clean coins than eighty that burn,” he says at last, and gives you your five.

lied.text: Ziyad pays eighty coins and drags the boat to the water. Mukhtar presses five coins into your hand, delighted.

honest: Told Ziyad the truth about the boat

a.text: Ziyad stands by an empty mooring. “She sank in the night. A soft plank by the keel - it went right through. You turned her over to clean her. You knew.”

choices.label: Admit it and offer to pay

paid.text: Ziyad takes the thirty coins without a word. Then he nods once. “That is more than most would do.”

denied.text: Ziyad says nothing. By evening the whole shore knows.

admitted: Sold a rotten boat - then paid for it
